summary: DoRaa Sangam House is a frontend-first luxury e-commerce single-page application built with React + TypeScript and Tailwind/shadcn-ui. It showcases a premium Banarasi saree catalog using in-repo dummy data, featuring a cinematic fixed canvas OceanBackground across all routes, a hero slider with layered animations, Banarasi collection showcases and carousels, product quick view and full-screen product detail overlays, wishlist and cart state persisted to localStorage, and a simulated guest checkout that generates an order ID and clears the cart. Storefront authentication is implemented client-side via a simulated OTP flow (+91 input, 6-digit OTP via alert/console, 3-attempt lockout with 10-minute timer, return-path + flash messaging) with an Internet Identity fallback. An admin panel exists with Internet Identity login and a principal-based gate, and supports in-memory product CRUD with multi-image previews and save feedback toasts/animations. A Motoko backend canister provides role-based access control (admin/user/guest) plus authenticated user-profile read/write and an admin-only deployment confirmation endpoint, though most storefront/admin data is not yet persisted to or read from the backend.

existing_features.title: Replace the existing plain phone number <Input> on the /login page with an advanced international phone input that has: (1) a left-side country selector showing flag + country name + dial code, and (2) a right-side phone number input. The dropdown must include at least 20 popular countries (including India +91, United States +1, United Kingdom +44, UAE +971) and support searching to manually change the country.

Auto-detect and pre-select the user's country on /login page load using a browser-based approach (e.g., Intl / locale hints). If detection fails or produces an unsupported/unknown country, default to India (+91). The selected flag + dial code must be shown immediately without user interaction.

Implement per-country phone validation triggered on blur of the phone field and on 'Send OTP' click. Validation must check that the number matches the selected country's expected length/format (e.g., India must validate as a 10-digit national number) and block OTP sending when invalid. Display an inline error message directly below the phone input group with exact text: "Please enter a valid [country] mobile number" (country name based on current selection).

Update /login page styling for the new phone input so it matches the existing dark luxury theme: black/dark backgrounds, pearl-blue (#7FB3D5) accents, and gold (#D4AF37) hover/glow on the dropdown and Send OTP button. Ensure the Send OTP button retains the existing continuous gold pulse/glow behavior and the phone input group is fully responsive (full-width on mobile, no overflow).

Keep the existing OTP login flow behavior intact: Send OTP → simulated OTP alert/console → OTP input → verify → success navigates to /dashboard; lockout/attempt handling must continue to work. The stored phone number used by the OTP session must include the selected international dial code (E.164-style with leading '+').

Add a brief internal QA checklist for this change (can be appended to frontend/RELEASE_NOTES.md for the next version) that confirms: auto-detection fallback to India works, dropdown shows flags/names/codes and manual selection works, validation is per-country, no UI/hover/animation regressions, and the OTP flow still works end-to-end.

architectural_notes: Custom lightweight SPA routing implemented via History API (useSpaLocation) with a custom browser event broadcast to synchronize navigation across multiple hook instances (no React Router).

The app shell is assembled via conditional route rendering in App.tsx (storefront, /login, /dashboard protected route, /admin/* with gate), and mounts OceanBackground as a persistent fixed layer behind all screens and overlays.
UI is composed with Tailwind CSS + shadcn/ui primitives; design tokens use OKLCH CSS variables, with many bespoke luxury micro-interactions (glows, ripples, wipe transitions, skeleton shimmer).
Accessibility pattern: all major animations and autoplay behaviors are gated by prefers-reduced-motion (usePrefersReducedMotion) with static/simplified fallbacks.

Client state is split into: (1) CommerceProvider cart context persisted to localStorage with derived totals; (2) wishlist localStorage hook; (3) admin products provider using in-memory React state only.
TanStack React Query is used as a data façade for dummy products, cart mutations, and simulated checkout; query invalidation is used to refresh dependent state after mutations.

Authentication is hybrid: OTP sessions persisted in localStorage for storefront, and Internet Identity (AuthClient) as a stronger identity option used for dashboard/admin; redirect-to-login uses flash message + return path stored in localStorage.

Backend integration pattern: identity-aware actor creation via useActor (React Query cached by principal) and backend-side access control initialization using a secret token obtained from the URL hash/session helper.
Motoko backend uses a mixin approach (MixinAuthorization) to inject access-control methods into the main actor and enforces permissions by trapping on unauthorized access.

Login page phone input may use a dedicated library (e.g., react-phone-input-2 or intl-tel-input) or custom component; should support country auto-detection (Intl API or lightweight geo lookup with fallback to India +91) and per-country validation integrated into existing OTP flow.
known_issues: Backend is only partially integrated with the frontend: products, orders, checkout, and admin CRUD are not persisted to or fetched from the Motoko canister; useGetOrders returns an empty array and useRegisterUser is a no-op.

Admin access is controlled by a hardcoded ADMIN_PRINCIPAL (currently set to the anonymous principal '2vxsx-fae'), which makes admin access impossible until configured to a real principal; docs also mention different testing principals, indicating configuration drift.
Simulated OTP UX uses window.alert and console logging to expose the OTP, and OTP validation is entirely client-side (no SMS delivery/server-side verification).

Type-model mismatch remains: React Query product/cart types use bigint while the UI generally consumes DUMMY_PRODUCTS (number/string IDs). This increases conversion complexity for future backend wiring.
React Query cart queryKey includes the cart array reference (['cart', cart]) which can cause cache churn and unnecessary re-renders/refetches as the array identity changes.
There appear to be two different index.css files (frontend/index.css and frontend/src/index.css); only src/index.css is imported in main.tsx, so the root-level CSS may be stale/unused and confusing.
frontend/src/components/SangamBackground.tsx is present but empty/placeholder despite summaries suggesting an implementation, indicating dead code or an incomplete migration.
Admin ImageDropzone uses window.alert for invalid file-type feedback, inconsistent with the premium toast system used elsewhere.
Some timers are typed as NodeJS.Timeout in browser code (e.g., carousel autoplay), which can cause typing friction depending on TS lib configuration.
useLocalStorageState’s setter closes over state (dependency on state), which can be error-prone under rapid successive updates compared to a ref-based implementation.
